name: Litify
description: Litify is a Salesforce-based legal operating platform for law firms and corporate legal departments, covering intake, matter management, document management, time and billing, spend management, reporting, analytics, AI workflows, and legal operations.
agentUseSummary: Litify is visible as a preview-only Marketplace entry. Litify publicly describes itself as built on Salesforce and AWS, with legal workflows, integrations, an open platform, comprehensive API toolkit, and partner ecosystem, but the reviewed public materials do not publish the concrete Litify-specific integration contract Relay needs: enrollment, authorization model, Salesforce connected-app requirements, package/object schema, least-privilege scopes, endpoint boundaries, tenant binding, rate limits, audit obligations, sandbox org, or production acceptance. Relay will not treat a generic Salesforce OAuth grant, Litify support login access, browser sessions, or Salesforce admin configuration as authorization to access Litify legal-practice data.

capabilities.label: Coordinate legal operations
capabilities.description: Preview a future Litify-approved, exact-org-authorized, least-privilege integration surface without assuming access to Salesforce org identity, matters, documents, billing, AI, or analytics data.

Litify remains visible for discovery, but no Hermes tools are callable before Litify approval, exact Salesforce-org authorization, least-privilege design review, and live acceptance.

providerSetup.blocker: Litify public materials describe Salesforce/AWS architecture, integrations, an open platform, comprehensive API toolkit, and partner ecosystem, but do not publish the complete Litify-specific connected-app, object model, permission, sandbox, rate-limit, audit, or production acceptance contract Relay requires.
providerSetup.nextAction: Ask Litify to approve Relay and provide the current Salesforce/Litify integration contract, connected-app requirements, sandbox org, production and test origins, package/object schema, permission sets, OAuth scopes, tenant binding, token lifecycle, rate limits, audit obligations, and live acceptance process. Then obtain explicit authorization from the exact customer org and approve a least-privilege action/data classification before implementing any connector.

evidence.supports: Litify describes an all-in-one legal platform covering intake management, matter management, document management, time and billing, spend management, reporting and analytics, AI workflows, and enterprise-grade security.

Litify states that it leverages Salesforce, adds legal-specific functionality, and offers an open platform, comprehensive API toolkit, extensive partner network, and enterprise Salesforce security controls.

Litify explains that customer data is stored in Salesforce data centers, documents are managed on AWS through Docrio, Litify personnel do not access customer databases without strict approval, and third parties are not allowed to access customer information within Litify.
Litify describes Salesforce's legal team using Litify for matters, invoices, outside-counsel spend, firm relationships, structured intake, collaboration, and performance insight.

securityNotes: No Litify account, Salesforce org, connected app, OAuth token, package metadata, firm identifier, matter, client, medical, document, billing, spend, AI, analytics, or legal-practice data was collected or tested.
A generic Salesforce API surface does not establish Relay authorization for Litify-specific objects, permission sets, Docrio documents, AI workflows, or legal-practice records.

Relay will not use browser sessions, Salesforce admin access, support login access, passwords, cookies, provider consoles, SOQL/SOSL exploration, traffic capture, scraping, or reverse engineering as a substitute for a Litify-approved integration contract.

All identity, client, intake, matter, medical, document, calendar, task, communication, time, billing, spend, invoice, reporting, analytics, AI, write, administration, raw API, pagination, bulk, and export operations remain unavailable.
